sentence_stem: When I was a child, I used to
correct_completion: play in the park every day.
full_sentence: When I was a child, I used to play in the park every day.
acceptable_variants: ride my bike around the neighborhood.
spend hours outside with my friends.

options.text: playing in the park every day.
options.why_wrong: 'Used to' is followed by the base form of the verb, not the -ing form. The -ing form appears after 'be used to' (meaning 'be familiar with').

options.text: plays in the park every day.
options.why_wrong: The -s ending belongs to the present simple with he, she or it. After 'used to' we always use the base form of the verb.

options.text: play in the park every day.
to play in the park every day.
options.why_wrong: 'Used to' is followed directly by the base verb. Adding 'to' before the verb creates an incorrect structure.

grammar_focus: 'used to' + base form of the verb for past habits
explanation: 'Used to' describes a past habit or routine that no longer happens, and it is always followed by the base form of the verb. Turkish speakers often express past habits with a past tense and a time expression, so they may be tempted to add an ending to the verb here.
translation: Ben çocukken her gün parkta oynardım.
